ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 3×3 grid. The number 2 has already been written in the upper-left cell; the number 3 has already been written in the cell in the second row and third column, that is, the middle-right cell. Reasoning: Suppose the sum of any two edge-adjacent cells equals the same constant. If three cells form a two-step path continuously along edges, denoted A-B-C, then A+B and B+C both equal this constant, so A=C. Therefore, after coloring like a chessboard, all cells of the same color have the same number, and all cells of the other color also have the same number. The upper-left cell belongs to the color class containing 5 cells, so these 5 cells all equal 2. The cell in the second row and third column belongs to the opposite color class containing 4 cells, so these 4 cells all equal 3. The total sum is 5×2+4×3=10+12=22.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a 3 by 3 grid with 2 in the top-left cell and 3 in the middle-right cell. From the text, impose that every pair of edge-adjacent cells has the same sum. Color the grid like a checkerboard: in any path of two edge steps, the first and third cells must be equal because both form the same sum with the middle cell. Therefore all cells of one checkerboard color are equal and all cells of the other color are equal. The top-left cell belongs to the 5-cell color class, so those five cells are 2. The middle-right cell belongs to the opposite 4-cell color class, so those four cells are 3. Add them: 5·2 + 4·3 = 22.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a 3 by 3 array with the top-left cell equal to 2 and the right cell of the middle row equal to 3. Let the common adjacent-cell sum be S. Name the top-middle cell x. Since it touches the top-left 2, S = 2 + x. The top-right cell touches the top-middle, so it must be S - x = 2. The middle-right cell touches the top-right cell and is shown as 3, so S = 2 + 3 = 5. Hence x = 3. Now propagate the same rule through the grid: every neighbor of a 2 must be 3 and every neighbor of a 3 must be 2. This fills the 3 by 3 grid in an alternating pattern with five 2s and four 3s, giving total 10 + 12 = 22.
